Acne.description: A common skin condition caused by clogged hair follicles, leading to pimples, blackheads, and whiteheads, most often on the face, chest, and back.
Acne.recommended_action: Mild cases can often be managed at home. See a dermatologist if it's severe, painful, or leaving scars.
general_treatment_info: Over-the-counter benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid

Actinic_Keratosis.description: A rough, scaly patch on sun-exposed skin caused by years of UV exposure. Considered precancerous since a small percentage can progress to skin cancer if untreated.
common_symptoms: Found on face, ears, scalp, hands
Actinic_Keratosis.recommended_action: See a dermatologist for evaluation. Not an emergency, but shouldn't be ignored.
general_treatment_info: Regular sun protection to prevent new lesions

Benign_tumors.description: Non-cancerous skin growths such as lipomas, fibromas, and similar lumps. Generally harmless but sometimes removed for comfort or cosmetic reasons.
common_symptoms: Soft or firm lump under the skin
Benign_tumors.recommended_action: Usually no action needed. See a doctor if it grows quickly, becomes painful, or changes in appearance.
general_treatment_info: No treatment necessary in most cases

Bullous.description: A group of conditions causing large, fluid-filled blisters on the skin, often related to autoimmune disease or infection.
common_symptoms: Itching or burning before blisters appear
Can affect mouth and other mucous membranes
Bullous.recommended_action: See a doctor promptly — bullous disorders often need proper diagnosis and monitoring.

Candidiasis.description: A fungal infection caused by Candida yeast, leading to red, itchy, inflamed skin, most common in warm, moist areas of the body.
common_symptoms: Sometimes with small pustules at the edges
Candidiasis.recommended_action: Often manageable with antifungal treatment. See a doctor if it doesn't improve or keeps recurring.
general_treatment_info: Keeping the area clean and dry
Oral antifungal medication for persistent cases

DrugEruption.description: A skin rash that occurs as a reaction to a medication, ranging from mild to potentially serious.
common_symptoms: Onset after starting a new medication
DrugEruption.recommended_action: See a doctor, especially if you've recently started a new medication. Seek urgent care if you have fever, blistering, or difficulty breathing.
general_treatment_info: Stopping the triggering medication (under medical guidance)

Eczema.description: A common condition causing dry, itchy, inflamed patches of skin, often linked to allergies or a sensitive skin barrier.
common_symptoms: Small raised bumps that may leak fluid
Eczema.recommended_action: Usually manageable at home. See a dermatologist if it persists beyond two weeks or worsens.

Infestations_Bites.description: Skin reactions caused by insect bites or infestations such as scabies or lice, typically causing itching and irritation.
common_symptoms: Sometimes in a line or cluster pattern
Intense itching, often worse at night for scabies
Infestations_Bites.recommended_action: Mild bites usually resolve on their own. See a doctor for suspected scabies or widespread infestation, since it can require prescription treatment.

Lichen.description: An inflammatory condition causing itchy, flat-topped purplish bumps, thought to be related to immune system activity.
common_symptoms: Can appear on skin, mouth, or nails
Lace-like white patches in the mouth (if oral)
Lichen.recommended_action: See a dermatologist for confirmation and management, especially if it's widespread or affecting the mouth.
general_treatment_info: Regular monitoring since it can be chronic

Lupus.description: An autoimmune condition that can cause distinctive skin rashes, often including a butterfly-shaped rash across the cheeks and nose.
common_symptoms: Red, scaly rash, often on the face
Rash may worsen with sun exposure
Lupus.recommended_action: See a doctor for proper evaluation — cutaneous lupus often requires coordinated care with a rheumatologist or dermatologist.
general_treatment_info: Sun protection (a key part of management)

Moles.description: Common, typically harmless skin growths formed by clusters of pigment cells. Most adults have several.
common_symptoms: Even color: tan, brown, or black
Usually smaller than 6mm and stable over time
Moles.recommended_action: No action typically needed. Use the ABCDE rule (Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter, Evolving) to monitor and see a dermatologist if any of these change.
general_treatment_info: No treatment necessary for typical moles
Prompt evaluation for any mole that changes

Psoriasis.description: A chronic condition causing the rapid buildup of skin cells, resulting in thick, scaly patches, often on elbows, knees, and scalp.
common_symptoms: Thick, red patches with silvery scales
Dry, cracked skin that may bleed
Psoriasis.recommended_action: See a dermatologist for diagnosis and a management plan, since psoriasis is a long-term condition.
general_treatment_info: Topical corticosteroids and vitamin D analogues

Rosacea.description: A chronic condition causing facial redness and visible blood vessels, sometimes with small red bumps resembling acne.
Rosacea.recommended_action: See a dermatologist for a management plan, especially if it's affecting your confidence or comfort.
general_treatment_info: Identifying and avoiding personal triggers (sun, spicy food, alcohol)
Laser treatment for visible blood vessels in some cases

Seborrh_Keratoses.description: Common, harmless skin growths that often appear with age, looking waxy or 'stuck-on'. Sometimes mistaken for warts or cancerous lesions.
Seborrh_Keratoses.recommended_action: Generally no treatment needed. Have a dermatologist confirm it isn't something else if it changes, bleeds, or looks unusual.
general_treatment_info: No treatment necessary if confirmed benign
Cryotherapy or removal if irritated or for cosmetic reasons

SkinCancer.description: A serious condition where skin cells grow abnormally and uncontrollably. Includes several types, some more aggressive than others. Early detection significantly improves outcomes.
common_symptoms: A new or changing mole or growth
SkinCancer.recommended_action: Seek an in-person dermatologist evaluation as soon as possible. This result should always be verified by a medical professional and is not a diagnosis.
general_treatment_info: Mohs micrographic surgery for certain areas/types
Radiation or topical therapy in specific cases
Immunotherapy or targeted therapy for advanced cases
Regular full-body skin checks after treatment

Sun_Sunlight_Damage.description: Changes to the skin from cumulative sun exposure, including discoloration, texture changes, and premature aging. Can increase risk of precancerous and cancerous changes over time.
Sun_Sunlight_Damage.recommended_action: Not urgent, but a good reason to see a dermatologist for a baseline skin check, since sun damage raises long-term skin cancer risk.
general_treatment_info: Professional treatments (chemical peels, laser) for cosmetic improvement
Regular skin checks given increased risk

Tinea.description: A common fungal skin infection causing a ring-shaped, itchy rash. Despite the name, it's not caused by a worm.
common_symptoms: Clearer skin in the center of the ring
Tinea.recommended_action: Usually treatable with antifungal medication. See a doctor if it doesn't improve or covers a large area.
general_treatment_info: Keeping the area clean and dry
Oral antifungal medication for widespread or stubborn cases
Avoiding sharing towels/clothing to prevent spread

Vascular_Tumors.description: Growths formed by abnormal blood vessels, such as hemangiomas, resulting in red, purple, or blue marks on the skin.
Vascular_Tumors.recommended_action: Usually harmless and often cosmetic. See a doctor if it bleeds easily, grows rapidly, or is painful.
general_treatment_info: Monitoring for changes in size or color

Vasculitis.description: Inflammation of blood vessels that can cause visible skin changes, including rashes, spots, or ulcers, sometimes linked to an underlying autoimmune or systemic condition.
common_symptoms: Small red or purple spots (often on legs)
Rash that doesn't fade when pressed
Sometimes accompanied by fatigue or joint pain
Vasculitis.recommended_action: See a doctor promptly for evaluation, as vasculitis can sometimes indicate a broader underlying condition.
general_treatment_info: Immune-suppressing medication in more serious cases

Vitiligo.description: A condition causing patches of skin to lose their pigment, resulting in smooth white patches, due to the loss of pigment-producing cells.
common_symptoms: White or light patches of skin
Can appear anywhere on the body
Patches may grow or spread over time
Premature whitening of hair in affected areas
Vitiligo.recommended_action: Not medically urgent, but see a dermatologist for confirmation and to discuss options if it's affecting your confidence.
general_treatment_info: Topical corticosteroids or other prescribed creams

Warts.description: Small, rough skin growths caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV), commonly appearing on hands or feet.
common_symptoms: May have tiny black dots (clotted blood vessels)
Can be itchy or slightly tender
May spread with contact or scratching
Warts.recommended_action: Many warts resolve on their own over time. See a doctor if it's painful, spreading, or doesn't improve with at-home treatment.
general_treatment_info: Avoiding picking or scratching to prevent spread
